literal: Regulations were set forth in brilliant order, all conforming to rule.
idiomatic: Regulations were set forth in brilliant order, all conforming to rule.

literal: Xiaowen issued an edict of praise and promulgated it throughout the realm, exactly as Jian had submitted.
idiomatic: Xiaowen issued an edict of praise and promulgated it throughout the realm, exactly as Jian had submitted.

literal: The people of Qi loved to sing of it, all saying their ears and eyes were renewed.
idiomatic: The people of Qi loved to sing of it, all saying their ears and eyes had been renewed.

literal: He and Jian's son Bochong both pressed to inherit; an edict allowed He to inherit, and he held the post of Governor of Dongjun.
idiomatic: He and Jian's son Bochong both pressed to inherit; an edict allowed He to inherit, and he held the post of Governor of Dongjun.

literal: Earlier, Sun Tian'en of the commandery was a wealthy magnate; he had once disputed land with He, and sent slave retainers who beat He nearly to death.
idiomatic: Earlier Sun Tian'en of the commandery was a wealthy magnate. He had once disputed land with He and sent slave retainers who beat He nearly to death.

literal: Now He accused Tian'en and his sons and brothers of trafficking with northern bandits; father, sons, and brothers were executed together, and property, goods, fields, and houses were all confiscated.
idiomatic: Now He accused Tian'en and his sons and brothers of trafficking with northern bandits. Father, sons, and brothers were executed together, and property, goods, fields, and houses were all confiscated.

literal: Tian'en's clansmen wished to go to court to plead injustice, but because He was kin to Yuan Cha they dared not lodge a complaint.
idiomatic: Tian'en's clansmen wished to go to court to plead injustice, but because He was kin to Yuan Cha they dared not lodge a complaint.

literal: He told men of his commandery: "If I sought a whole province, I could probably get one.
idiomatic: He told men of his commandery: "If I sought a whole province, I could probably get one.

literal: Thinking of this petty man, the pain goes to the marrow—so I begged this commandery to repay an old grudge; after this I will seek no more wealth or rank.
idiomatic: Thinking of this petty man, the pain goes to the marrow—so I begged this commandery to repay an old grudge. After this I will seek no more wealth or rank.

literal: " Men of insight said: "The prince will perish in this place!
idiomatic: " Men of insight said: "The prince will perish in this place!

literal: " He died; posthumously made Governor of Xiang Province.
idiomatic: " He died and was posthumously made Governor of Xiang Province.

literal: Prince of Hejian Xiu was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian, Xiu, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

literal: He died without sons; Taiwu decreed that Prince of Henan Yao's son Jie'er should inherit, and his fief was changed to Prince of Lüeyang.
idiomatic: He died without sons. Taiwu decreed that the Prince of Henan Yao's son Jie'er should inherit, and his fief was changed to Prince of Lüeyang.

literal: In the beginning of Zhengping he was guilty and granted death; the title was abolished.
idiomatic: In the beginning of Zhengping he was guilty and granted death; the title was abolished.

literal: Prince of Changle Chuwén was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: The Prince of Changle, Chuwén, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

literal: Clever and eloquent from youth.
idiomatic: Clever and eloquent from youth.

literal: At fourteen he died.
idiomatic: At fourteen he died.

literal: Mingyuan grieved deeply; from the small coffin of catalpa to the burial he often came in person to mourn.
idiomatic: Mingyuan grieved deeply. From the small catalpa coffin to the burial he often came in person to mourn.

literal: Buried beside Jinling; no sons; title abolished.
idiomatic: He was buried beside Jinling. Having no sons, the title was abolished.

literal: Prince of Guangping Lian was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping, Lian, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

literal: He died without sons; Taiwu made Prince of Yangping Xi's second son Hun Prince of Nanping to continue Lian's line.
idiomatic: He died without sons. Taiwu made the Prince of Yangping Xi's second son Hun Prince of Nanping to continue Lian's line.

literal: Hun loved bow and horse; shooting birds he would strike them in flight one after another, and in a day shoot fifty hares.
idiomatic: Hun loved bow and horse. Shooting birds he would strike them in flight one after another, and in a day shoot fifty hares.

literal: Taiwu once ordered attendants to shoot in turns; the winner filled the tally; he ordered Hun to release, and three shots all hit.
idiomatic: Taiwu once ordered attendants to shoot in turns; the winner filled the tally. He ordered Hun to release, and three shots all hit.

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, valued his skill, and often kept him at his side.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, valued his skill, and often kept him at his side.

literal: He rose repeatedly to Commander of Liang Province, Commander-in-Chief of Western Rong, and Colonel Protecting the Western Regions; his grace was felt throughout Liang.
idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Commander of Liang Province, Commander-in-Chief of Western Rong, and Colonel Protecting the Western Regions; his grace was felt throughout Liang.

literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, elders wept and followed to send him off, as if parting from kin.
idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, elders wept and followed to send him off, as if parting from kin.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Fei inherited.
idiomatic: His son Fei inherited.

literal: Later he was granted the name Xiao.
idiomatic: Later he was granted the name Xiao.

literal: Nine feet tall, a belt ten spans round, imposing in appearance, with refined bearing.
idiomatic: Nine feet tall, a belt ten spans round, imposing in appearance, with refined bearing.

literal: Upright and pure, he loved straight speech and remonstrance; court ministers feared him.
idiomatic: Upright and pure, he loved straight speech and remonstrance; court ministers feared him.

literal: Xiaowen especially favored him and appointed him Director of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: Xiaowen especially favored him and appointed him Director of the Imperial Clan.

literal: An edict said: "From now on in memorials, ministers addressing one another may give their names;
idiomatic: An edict said: "From now on in memorials, ministers addressing one another may give their names;

literal: only the Prince of Nanping alone may speak his title directly.
idiomatic: only the Prince of Nanping alone may speak his title directly.

literal: " He was promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace.
idiomatic: " He was promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace.

literal: He died and was granted the first-grade secret coffin of the Eastern Garden.
idiomatic: He died and was granted the first-grade secret coffin of the Eastern Garden.

literal: Xiaowen wore unhemmed mourning at Xiao's funeral, held no banquets, posthumous title Prince An.
idiomatic: Xiaowen wore unhemmed mourning at Xiao's funeral and held no banquets. He was posthumously titled Prince An.

literal: His son Zuan inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited.

literal: Prince of Jingzhao Li was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: The Prince of Jingzhao, Li, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Tuxiang inherited; his fief was changed to Prince of Jiangyang.
idiomatic: His son Tuxiang inherited; his fief was changed to Prince of Jiangyang.

literal: He died without sons.
idiomatic: He died without sons.

literal: Emperor Xianwen made Prince of Nanping Xiao's second son Ji, styled Shiren, his heir; he inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen made the Prince of Nanping Xiao's second son Ji, styled Shiren, his heir; he inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he served as Governor of Qing Province.

literal: A household slave took a man's daughter as wife and concubine, and also took free persons as maidservants; the censor impeached him and he was stripped of office and title.
idiomatic: A household slave took a man's daughter as wife and concubine, and also took free persons as maidservants. The censor impeached him and he was stripped of office and title.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, Ji's son Cha had first taken the dowager's younger sister; Ji recovered his original fief;
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, Ji's son Cha had first taken the dowager's younger sister; Ji recovered his original fief;

literal: later his fief was changed to Prince of Jingzhao; he held the posts of Minister of State and was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: later his fief was changed to Prince of Jingzhao. He held the posts of Minister of State and was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

literal: Ji, already holding prominent posts inside and outside under Xiaowen, when Ling came to court entered the inner circle of trust and rose through the high offices.
idiomatic: Ji, already holding prominent posts inside and outside under Xiaowen, when Ling came to court entered the inner circle of trust and rose through the high offices.

literal: He repeatedly memorialized to yield his post, was transferred to Grand Guardian, Palace Attendant as before, with drums before and behind added.
idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized to yield his post, was transferred to Grand Guardian, Palace Attendant as before, with drums before and behind added.

literal: An edict said that at the great festivals, when rites require court celebration, Ji by his high rank and long years might follow the precedent of Prince of Qijun Jian—after court he was led to sit, exempt from bowing and prostration.
idiomatic: An edict said that at the great festivals, when rites require court celebration, Ji by his high rank and long years might follow the precedent of Prince of Qijun Jian—after court he was led to sit, exempt from bowing and prostration.

literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant as before.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant as before.

literal: At that time Cha held the power of life and death; on the day of Ji's appointment those who escorted him filled the court, and men of insight were afraid for him.
idiomatic: At that time Cha held the power of life and death. On the day of Ji's appointment those who escorted him filled the court, and men of insight were afraid for him.

literal: Another edict allowed him to ride in a hand-drawn carriage to the hall, two men supporting him, ceremony equal to the Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang.
idiomatic: Another edict allowed him to ride in a hand-drawn carriage to the hall, two men supporting him, ceremony equal to the Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang.

literal: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander, and Commander of Western Route Military Affairs.
idiomatic: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Commander, and Commander of Western Route Military Affairs.

literal: When the army set out the emperor came to feast him; the whole court saw him off.
idiomatic: When the army set out the emperor came to feast him; the whole court saw him off.

literal: Soon he was given the additional title Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional title Grand Commandant.

literal: When the army returned Ji memorialized asking to restore the fief of Jiangyang; the edict assented.
idiomatic: When the army returned Ji memorialized asking to restore the fief of Jiangyang; the edict assented.

literal: In his later years Ji grew greedier; governors, prefects, and magistrates newly appointed to office—all received his bribes as entrustment.
idiomatic: In his later years Ji grew greedier. Governors, prefects, and magistrates newly appointed to office—all received his bribes as entrustment.

literal: Wife and sons each made separate requests; even clerks of commanderies and counties could not choose fairly.
idiomatic: Wife and sons each made separate requests; even clerks of commanderies and counties could not choose fairly.

literal: Relying on Cha's power, judicial officers dared not investigate; the realm suffered under it.
idiomatic: Relying on Cha's power, judicial officers dared not investigate; the realm suffered under it.

literal: When Cha was dismissed, Ji was confined at home.
idiomatic: When Cha was dismissed, Ji was confined at home.

literal: At first, when Erzhu Rong was in the Direct Attendance, he several times presented famous horses to Cha; Cha received him with favor, and Rong was deeply grateful.
idiomatic: At first, when Erzhu Rong was in the Direct Attendance, he several times presented famous horses to Cha. Cha received him with favor, and Rong was deeply grateful.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was again made Ji's Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was again made Ji's Grand Preceptor and Governor of Si Province.

literal: In the first year of Yong'an he died; posthumously granted the golden axe, Commander of Nine Provinces, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Chancellor as before—posthumous title Prince Wulie.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yong'an he died. He was posthumously granted the golden axe, Commander of Nine Provinces, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand Chancellor as before—posthumous title Prince Wulie.

literal: Cha, styled Bojun, childhood name Yecha.
idiomatic: Cha, styled Bojun, childhood name Yecha.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, as Cha's brother-in-law he was made Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling came to court, as Cha's brother-in-law he was made Regular Attendant.

literal: Cha's wife was enfeoffed Lady of Xinping, later Lady of Fengyi, and made Lady Attendant of the Palace.
idiomatic: Cha's wife was enfeoffed Lady of Xinping, later Lady of Fengyi, and made Lady Attendant of the Palace.

literal: Cha's daughter died young; Ling issued an edict enfeoffing her as District Lady.
idiomatic: Cha's daughter died young; Ling issued an edict enfeoffing her as District Lady.

literal: Cha was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards.
idiomatic: Cha was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Commander of the Guards.

literal: Once in the Gate Department he also held overall command of the forbidden troops and was deeply trusted by Ling.
idiomatic: Once in the Gate Department he also held overall command of the forbidden troops and was deeply trusted by Ling.

literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, as a kinsman and worthy man assisting in government, often wished to remove him.
idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, as a kinsman and worthy man assisting in government, often wished to remove him.

literal: Cha then had Regular Attendant Song Wei report that Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu plotted treason to set up Yi; Yi was confined.
idiomatic: Cha then had Regular Attendant Song Wei report that Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu plotted treason to set up Yi. Yi was confined.

literal: Later exhaustive investigation found no truth; though Yi was released he was still guarded by troops in a separate lodge west of the palace.
idiomatic: Later exhaustive investigation found no truth. Though Yi was released he was still guarded by troops in a separate lodge west of the palace.

literal: After a long while Cha feared Yi would in the end harm him; with Palace Attendant Liu Teng he secretly plotted, falsely taking the chief food-service eunuchs Hu Du and Hu Ding to accuse Yi: "He bribed Du and others with gold and silk to place poison in the imperial food to harm the emperor.
idiomatic: After a long while Cha feared Yi would in the end harm him. With Palace Attendant Liu Teng he secretly plotted, falsely taking the chief food-service eunuchs Hu Du and Hu Ding to accuse Yi: "He bribed Du and others with gold and silk to place poison in the imperial food to harm the emperor.

literal: " Teng memorialized with the full report.
idiomatic: " Teng memorialized with the full report.

literal: Emperor Ming believed it; he then held court at Xianyang Hall.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming believed it; he then held court at Xianyang Hall.

literal: Teng closed the Eternal Lane gate; the empress dowager could not go out.
idiomatic: Teng closed the Eternal Lane gate; the empress dowager could not go out.

literal: Yi entered and met Cha behind Hanzhang Hall; he ordered clan guards and direct attendants to seize Yi's sleeves and bring him into the eastern office of Hanzhang.
idiomatic: Yi entered and met Cha behind Hanzhang Hall. He ordered clan guards and direct attendants to seize Yi's sleeves and bring him into the eastern office of Hanzhang.

literal: Teng claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to discuss, charging great treason.
idiomatic: Teng claimed an edict summoning the hundred officials to discuss, charging great treason.

literal: All feared Cha and none dared dissent.
idiomatic: All feared Cha and none dared dissent.

literal: Only Vice Director You Zhao held a different view.
idiomatic: Only Vice Director You Zhao held a different view.

literal: Cha and Teng took the ministers' discussion in to memorialize; in the middle of the night Yi was killed.
idiomatic: Cha and Teng took the ministers' discussion in to memorialize; in the middle of the night Yi was killed.

literal: Then they forged an edict in the empress dowager's name yielding power; Cha then with Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong and others assisted in government.
idiomatic: Then they forged an edict in the empress dowager's name yielding power. Cha then with Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong and others assisted in government.

literal: He constantly attended in the forbidden quarters; Ming called him Uncle by marriage.
idiomatic: He constantly attended in the forbidden quarters; Ming called him Uncle by marriage.

literal: After that the hundred officials trod on one another's heels.
idiomatic: After that the hundred officials trod on one another's heels.

literal: Later the emperor moved to Huiyin Hall; Cha also dwelt on the hall's right, flattering to the utmost, and went in and out of the forbidden quarters, always having brave men carry swords before and behind.
idiomatic: Later the emperor moved to Huiyin Hall; Cha also dwelt on the hall's right, flattering to the utmost, and went in and out of the forbidden quarters, always having brave men carry swords before and behind.

literal: Cha set wooden railings in the shed outside the Qianqiu Gate; when he went in or out he would rest there, with trusted guards against sudden attack.
idiomatic: Cha set wooden railings in the shed outside the Qianqiu Gate. When he went in or out he would rest there, with trusted guards against sudden attack.

literal: At first, when Cha held sole power, he feigned sentiment and adorned himself, laboring humbly to treat scholars.
idiomatic: At first, when Cha held sole power, he feigned sentiment and adorned himself, laboring humbly to treat scholars.

literal: Once he had his wish he turned arrogant and willful, addicted to wine and women, seizing and granting at whim.
idiomatic: Once he had his wish he turned arrogant and willful, addicted to wine and women, seizing and granting at whim.

literal: He made a separate treasury in the forbidden quarters and held it himself; treasures filled it.
idiomatic: He made a separate treasury in the forbidden quarters and held it himself; treasures filled it.

literal: Cha once had a woman lie in the food carriage covered with a quilt.
idiomatic: Cha once had a woman lie in the food carriage covered with a quilt.

literal: The carriage entered the inner quarters and left the same way; the guards knew but none dared speak.
idiomatic: The carriage entered the inner quarters and left the same way. The guards knew but none dared speak.

literal: Aunts, elder and younger sisters, and women—promiscuity without distinction.
idiomatic: Aunts, elder and younger sisters, and women—promiscuity without distinction.

literal: Government affairs languished; discipline was not upheld.
idiomatic: Government affairs languished; discipline was not upheld.

literal: Many provinces and garrisons had unfit men in office; then the realm fell into disorder.
idiomatic: Many provinces and garrisons had unfit men in office; then the realm fell into disorder.

literal: Cha knew himself unlawful and feared dismissal; he secretly sent his younger brother Hongye to summon men of Wu Province such as Ji Kugen to feast with him.
idiomatic: Cha knew himself unlawful and feared dismissal. He secretly sent his younger brother Hongye to summon men of Wu Province such as Ji Kugen to feast with him.

literal: They swore an oath, intending to stir rebellion so the court would surely appoint him Grand General to campaign; they would then act inside and outside together and so establish himself.
idiomatic: They swore an oath, intending to stir rebellion so the court would surely appoint him Grand General to campaign. They would then act inside and outside together and so establish himself.

literal: Kugen and the rest agreed; he richly rewarded Kugen and the rest and sent them back to the province to buy horses with Hongye.
idiomatic: Kugen and the rest agreed. He richly rewarded them and sent them back to the province to buy horses with Hongye.

literal: After Liu Teng died the guard grew somewhat slack.
idiomatic: After Liu Teng died the guard grew somewhat slack.

literal: Cha also grew somewhat at ease; he often lodged outside, going out every day to roam and lingering in other districts.
idiomatic: Cha also grew somewhat at ease. He often lodged outside, going out every day to roam and lingering in other districts.
